cases.user_request: I just created a CKS cluster and my API token is exported as CW_API_ACCESS_TOKEN. Get kubectl talking to the cluster.

rubric_criteria.desc: The agent states there is no coreweave CLI command and no Terraform data source or output that fetches a kubeconfig — CKS uses Managed Auth and the kubeconfig embeds the API access token as a static bearer token.

Because the token is already in the environment, the agent builds the kubeconfig itself (path A) from the token plus the API server endpoint (cks_api_server_endpoint output, Console page, or API) instead of sending the customer to the Console.

The agent never echoes the token value and writes the kubeconfig by letting the shell expand the variable (no logged heredoc with a pasted secret); file permissions are restricted (umask 077 / chmod 600).
The agent does not add insecure-skip-tls-verify: true; certificate errors are treated as a wrong endpoint or local trust-store problem, not a reason to disable TLS verification.
The agent verifies with kubectl get nodes and explains that a fresh cluster with no node pools may legitimately show zero nodes.

cases.user_request: How do I connect kubectl to my CoreWeave cluster? I don't have an API token yet.

rubric_criteria.desc: With no token available, the agent uses the Console path (Tokens page Create Token with Kubeconfig download, or Clusters page > More options > Download kubeconfig), states that an agent cannot click the download button, and pauses for the customer to download the file.
The agent warns that the kubeconfig from the Tokens page is shown/downloadable only once.

The agent points KUBECONFIG at the downloaded file and — because a CoreWeave kubeconfig can carry contexts for multiple clusters — selects and confirms the right context (kubectl config get-contexts / use-context / current-context) before doing anything else.

The agent verifies with kubectl get nodes, interprets a rejected call as a token-access problem, and notes private clusters have no public endpoint (Console download may be unavailable; private access goes through CoreWeave Support).
